rows: Tell me what I missed. Then give me a chance to show you I heard.
Brawling is a fair tool when it is used well. Would you show me how you use it?
A gamble can teach me something. What would you like me to learn from yours?
Pace, for me, is a good pace for learning. Shall we go at that pace?
The people deserve a match worth their time. Would you help me give them that?
I would like a chance to prove I am ready.
I would like to be trusted to lead, and I know I still have to earn it.
Would you mark my stance for me? Does it look ready to you?
Technique, then? What would you change? What would you change in mine, if you could?
Strikes are part of learning the job. Tell me which ones you would start with.
A gamble should be something we can talk about after. Would you like to talk about yours?
A stall is something I am trying to avoid. Would you show me what you would do instead?
The people want to see a contest. Would you let me give them one?
Would you say I am among the best yet? What do you think I still need to learn?
Would you show me what makes your {strength} work? Would you show me what makes it work?
I have been trying to understand your {strength}, and I would like your help with it.
Would calm be the right approach, do you think? Okay. Would you show me how you did it?
Did that land for you? Thank you for saying that.
I could argue that. Would you like to test me on it instead?
Would you keep the count? Keep me down, and then tell me what I could do better.
On the mat I will ask you as I go. Tell me if I am wrong.
Grounded or standing, would you show me the next step?
Would you face me for a moment? I would like to learn from what you do.
Was that a proper answer? Thank you. Would you explain the reasoning?
I wonder if the question is still open. I would really like your answer, if you have one.
Did that land for you? I will try to remember that.
Could I accept that? Will you test me on it at the bell?
I will wrestle this match and I will listen to every correction you give me.
I hope my approach is careful enough. I hope you will see me try my best on the night.
Whatever happens, I hope you will tell me what I learned.
Is there more to come? I would like the chance to finish it well.
I have one more question for you, and I hope you will answer it when the bell rings.
You're right to ask me. I haven't got an example I can stand behind. I'd rather learn than pretend.
I shouldn't say something about you that I can't explain. Can we start with the wrestling instead?
Thank you for being clear about that. I'd rather learn what you can do than argue about something we can't establish.
Then I won't ask you to prove a negative. Let's find out what happens when we wrestle.
I'd like them to see whether I can adapt when you catch me making a mistake. That seems a fair test.
Can we let the match show what I've learned? I'd rather give them something they can judge for themselves.
